horoscopes.intro: November 11 in the stars: Find out what’s in store for you today in our daily horoscopes for Wednesday November 11. Read the daily horoscopes for your Sun sign or rising sign (ascendant) to plan your day.

aries.text: Widen your search parameters, Aries. The people you’re looking for are out there. You just need to go a bit further afield. Reach out to a long-distance colleague, since a short message could lead to anything from a fruitful Zoom meeting to a work trip you’d actually enjoy. With holiday travel season bearing down, now’s the moment to float those dates. Connecting with a broader range of people where you live can also open up unexpected possibilities, and a person with a very different backstory may provide the fresh perspective you need.

taurus.text: With the moon sauntering through your potent eighth house, your sultry intensity can magnetize someone you want to know better. Whether you’d like to get closer to a sexy love interest or a fascinating friend, quality one-on-one time is a must. Instead of angling for a moment alone at a group hang, suggest a private tête-à-tête so you can find out whether this person has the substance and depth to go the distance with you. Long November nights are ideal for this!

gemini.text: Table for two! The moon is darting through your partnership house today, persuading you to pair off for both business and pleasure. Join forces with a colleague on a project, even if it means giving up a little of your cherished freedom. Just make sure you’re on the same page when it comes to expectations and division of labor, and spell everything out in black and white to be on the safe side. After you clock out, unwind over a long dinner with someone who can flip as fast as you can from discussing global politics to the Real Housewives.

cancer.text: Your wellbeing is your most valuable asset, Cancer. With the moon in your salubrious sixth house, you’re reminded to give your routines the attention they deserve. Instead of reaching for sugary snacks and another cup of coffee to boost your energy, build the day around real meals that keep your fuel steady. Go for a walk, stretch between meetings and try to squeeze in a Spin class. If it’s getting dark early where you live, a short guided meditation will clear your head faster than scrolling will.

leo.text: Let your inner child out to play! The moon is skipping through your joyful fifth house, inspiring you to put your personal stamp on everything you do. Dive into a creative endeavor and welcome a visit from the muse. Express your singular style with a head-turning coat, since November is when outerwear becomes the entire outfit in some climates. The best accessory of all? Your own swooning heart on your leather bomber-jacket sleeve. Since the fifth house also rules romance, tonight was made for sweet amour. Whether you’re in a relationship or unattached, consider this your cue to flirt shamelessly.

virgo.text: While the moon slumbers in your comfy fourth house, working from home would be ideal today. If you must report for duty, stay cozy at the office with your favorite cardigan and mug—and maybe a scented candle if you’re allowed. Make a beeline for Chez Virgo after you log off and enjoy a delicious homemade dinner or some yummy takeout. If you feel like having some company, invite a mellow companion to join you for soup and something undemanding to watch together.

libra.text: Don’t try to figure it out all by yourself, Libra. If you’re spinning your wheels, reach out to someone who doesn’t have any stake in the issue. Maybe a new coworker, or the person you chat with occasionally while waiting for your coffee order, can offer objective input that doesn’t duplicate the track running on repeat in your head. You might need to brace yourself for feedback you weren’t expecting. Thank them for their honesty. It will help in the long run, even if it stings for a minute.

scorpio.text: Clarify what you really need, Scorpio. Don’t press someone for more when you’re not even sure what you’re after, since they can’t give you what you want if you don’t know what that is. As soon as you home in on your core requirements, you’ll be able to identify which pieces of the puzzle other people can provide for you. With less than two months left in the year, getting specific now pays off.

sagittarius.text: Make today all about you, Sag. While the moon hovers in your sign, you have planetary permission to put your own needs first. If that entails changing some tentative plans to suit your mood, no big deal, as long as you’re not ghosting anyone or leaving a loved one high and dry. Go where your curiosity takes you, and you might end up wandering through a photography exhibit or sampling fragrances in a shop you stumble across. Tonight could find you shooting pool at a funky dive bar or curled up on your couch with your dog. Your call!

capricorn.text: Shield your field, Capricorn. You’re the one everybody brings their problems to, but letting someone ramble on indefinitely while you absorb their stress like a sponge isn’t good for either of you. Resist the temptation to manage their situation and set some limits around your time and energy instead. Give kind advice, then step back. Figuring it out for themselves will allow them to grow—and with pre-holiday obligations already stacking up, it’ll save your sanity, too.

aquarius.text: Turn that solo project into a group endeavor while the moon glides through your collaborative eleventh house today. You’re surrounded by talented players who are ready and willing to team up with you. Rather than holding off until you’ve perfected your work, solicit input now, since the feedback you get could point toward the synergistic connections that await. Tonight was made for hanging with your whole squad—or an even bigger circle that includes some fresh faces. Keep plans casual, pick somewhere warm and see who shows up!

pisces.text: Stay visible and keep your eyes on the prize, whether that’s a coveted promotion, public acclaim or one more feather in your cap before the year runs out. You’re focused on success while the moon tours your tenth house of drive and fame today. Don’t be afraid to toot your own horn and liaise with the movers and shakers who can help you achieve what you’re aiming for. This is not the day for humble service, Pisces, so save the selfless routine for another time and show ’em what you’ve got!

items.title: Single-cell machine learning uncovers genetically anchored, cell-type specific programs of Alzheimer's disease
items.originalTitle: Single-cell machine learning uncovers genetically anchored, cell-type specific programs of Alzheimer's disease
items.summary: Univariate differential expression analysis dominates single-cell transcriptomic studies of Alzheimer's disease, yet marginal testing alone cannot resolve multivariate disease-associated structure or distinguish clinical from neuropathological signatures. 2 million nuclei from 627 donors.
items.caution: A link, not proof of cause.
items.abstract: Univariate differential expression analysis dominates single-cell transcriptomic studies of Alzheimer's disease, yet marginal testing alone cannot resolve multivariate disease-associated structure or distinguish clinical from neuropathological signatures. Here we introduce TriSCOPE, a framework integrating multivariate predictive modeling, donor-aware differential expression, and pseudotime inference, applied to six Alzheimer's disease snRNA-seq datasets comprising ~4.2 million nuclei from 627 donors. Across six major brain cell types and 41 subclusters, we identify cell-type-specific predictively expressed genes that are largely non-overlapping with differentially expressed genes, revealing disease-relevant signals invisible to univariate approaches. Conditional GWAS-eQTL colocalization anchors a subset of these predictively expressed genes to inherited Alzheimer's disease risk loci, including 27 genetically supported gene-cell type pairs (among them ARL17B, JAZF1) with no significant differential expression. Integration across all three analytical branches nominates high-confidence convergent programs including astrocytic stress markers (such as GFAP, MT2A), neuronal signaling genes (like RASGEF1B, LINGO1, NRG1), and microglial and oligodendrocyte regulators (including SYTL3, SPP1, APOD). Comparison of clinical and neuropathological models reveals cell-type-specific divergence between cognitive and pathological Alzheimer's disease signatures. Key predictively expressed genes including ARL17B, LINGO1, and APOE replicate across independent cohorts, with cross-cohort generalizability confirmed across all three analytical branches of TriSCOPE.

items.title: Evaluating Age-Related Motor System Changes Using Gait as a Functionally Relevant Marker
items.originalTitle: Evaluating Age-Related Motor System Changes Using Gait as a Functionally Relevant Marker
items.summary: Background and objectives: Aging causes gait and mobility decline, which often precedes cognitive impairment and dementia.
items.caution: A link, not proof of cause.
items.abstract:
Background and objectives: Aging causes gait and mobility decline, which often precedes cognitive impairment and dementia. Biological "age gaps" (the difference between biological and chronological age) are traditionally measured using neuroimaging and electroencephalography, quantified gait metrics have not been used for this purpose. We hypothesize that specific gait metrics can effectively quantify biological aging and predict future cognitive impairment risk.

Methods: We analyzed gait data from the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging, a population-based cohort in Olmsted County, MN. Participants without known gait disorder, recruited between 2007 and 2025, were included. We used these data to develop a machine learning-based age prediction model. This gait-based age prediction model was used to devise the "gait age gap," a quantified metric of gait abnormality defined as the difference between age as predicted by gait performance ("gait age") and chronological age. We used the gait age gap to evaluate the risk of future cognitive impairment.

Results: We analyzed 19,637 walk trials from 5,794 unique participants (49% female), with a mean age of 78 (±8) years. Gait age was primarily driven by changes in measures of stability. A larger gait age gap was associated with impaired cognitive and functional status. In longitudinal analysis, each gait age gap year exceeding chronological age increased the risk of converting from a normal to cognitively impaired (CI) state by 7% per year. Gait age gap outperformed baseline velocity in distinguishing normal from CI groups and was associated with future risk of conversion from normal to a CI state hazard ratio = 1.07 (95% CI 1.03-1.13) for gait age gap vs hazard ratio = 0.99 (95% CI 0.98-1.00) for velocity.

Discussion: The gait age gap is a functionally relevant marker of age-related motor system changes that quantifies deviations from expected gait performance for a given chronological age. It is associated with a higher risk of future cognitive impairment among cognitively normal individuals. This study includes a relatively homogeneous cohort of predominantly Caucasian participants. To assess generalizability and the trajectory of motoric aging across sociodemographic groups, these findings need to be replicated in diverse cohorts. Wearable sensor technologies could also make such measures more scalable.

items.title: Giant step-boundary-triggered nonlocal modulation of magnetization reversal in multi-stepped van der Waals ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2
items.originalTitle: Giant step-boundary-triggered nonlocal modulation of magnetization reversal in multi-stepped van der Waals ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2
items.summary: Control of magnetization reversal is crucial for spintronic memory and logic devices. Previous studies on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnets have largely treated magnetic regions in isolation, leaving the roles of step boundaries comparatively unexplored.
items.caution: A link, not proof of cause.
items.abstract: Control of magnetization reversal is crucial for spintronic memory and logic devices. Previous studies on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnets have largely treated magnetic regions in isolation, leaving the roles of step boundaries comparatively unexplored. Here, we investigate step-boundary-triggered nonlocal modulation of magnetization reversal in multi-stepped Fe3GaTe2 using Kerr microscopy, Lorentz transmission electron microscopy, and micromagnetic simulations. Our results indicate that step boundaries can serve as preferential sites for premature nucleation, giving rise to two distinct regimes. In Type I, reversal initiated in a thicker region propagates rapidly across the step boundary, reducing the coercivity of an adjacent thinner region by up to 59.3%. In Type II, stripe domains originating from the thicker region progressively enter the thinner region, shifting its critical switching field polarity and transforming its hysteresis loop from square to slanted, accompanied by a transition in the dominant reversal mode from rapid domain-wall motion to stripe domain growth. Similar behavior in Fe3GeTe2 suggests that step-boundary-mediated modulation may occur more broadly in layered van der Waals ferromagnets. Our findings highlight step engineering as a potential non-invasive strategy for designing efficient and thermally stable vdW spintronic devices.

items.title: Differences in Health and Access to Care Between Heterosexual and Sexual Minority Health Care Professionals
items.originalTitle: Differences in Health and Access to Care Between Heterosexual and Sexual Minority Health Care Professionals
items.summary: Importance: Little is known about the health and access to care of sexual minority health care professionals (HCPs). Objective: To compare health outcomes, health insurance coverage, and access to care between sexual minority and heterosexual HCPs.
items.caution: A link, not proof of cause.
items.abstract:
Importance: Little is known about the health and access to care of sexual minority health care professionals (HCPs).

Objective: To compare health outcomes, health insurance coverage, and access to care between sexual minority and heterosexual HCPs.

Design, setting, and participants: For this survey study, cross-sectional data analysis of the 2020, 2021, 2023, and 2024 National Health Interview Surveys was performed. The study population included nationally representative household probability samples of noninstitutionalized US civilian adults aged 18 years or older, restricted to HCPs working in health care settings. Data analysis was conducted between February 2024 and August 2026.

Exposure: Self-reported sexual orientation, categorized as sexual minority (gay, lesbian, bisexual, or another nonheterosexual identity) or heterosexual.

Main outcomes and measures: The main outcomes included cigarette smoking, lifetime diagnosis of depression, moderate to severe psychological distress, selected physical health conditions, primary source of health insurance coverage, and delayed or forgone medical care, mental health care, and prescription medications due to cost. Multivariable logistic regression models compared outcomes while adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics.

Results: The sample included 2890 HCPs (2731 heterosexual and 159 sexual minority; mean [SE] age, 44.9 [0.7] years; 74.7% [0.9%] female [survey weighted]). Sexual minority individuals represented 5.7% (95% CI, 4.8%-6.7%) of HCPs and were more likely to be younger (aged 26-34 years: 38.8% [95% CI, 30.1%-48.3%] vs 24.0% [95% CI, 22.2%-25.9%]), never married (32.7% [95% CI, 24.7%-41.8%] vs 14.6% [95% CI, 13.0%-16.4%]), and living in households below the federal poverty level (7.4% [95% CI, 3.4%-15.4%] vs 1.1% [95% CI, 0.7%-1.7%]) compared with heterosexual HCPs. Sexual minority HCPs were significantly more likely to report a lifetime diagnosis of depression (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 3.05 [95% CI, 2.02-4.59]), moderate to severe psychological distress (AOR, 2.06 [95% CI, 1.23-3.46]), arthritis (AOR, 2.45 [95% CI, 1.42-4.22]), and delayed medical care due to cost (AOR, 2.06 [95% CI, 1.14-3.72]). Sexual minority HCPs faced greater disparities in access to care: they were more likely to forgo mental health care (AOR, 3.74 [95% CI, 2.11-6.63]) and to forgo prescription medications (AOR, 4.81 [95% CI, 2.52-9.15]) due to cost than their heterosexual peers.

items.title: Physical exercise interventions to promote healthy ageing in older adults: from research to clinical implementation
items.originalTitle: Physical exercise interventions to promote healthy ageing in older adults: from research to clinical implementation
items.summary: Physical exercise interventions have emerged as a key strategy to promote healthy ageing; however, they remain insufficiently implemented in real-world contexts.
items.caution: A link, not proof of cause.
items.abstract: Physical exercise interventions have emerged as a key strategy to promote healthy ageing; however, they remain insufficiently implemented in real-world contexts. In this Series paper, we synthesised the current evidence on the effects of exercise interventions on functional ability and intrinsic capacity-the marker of healthy ageing defined by WHO that encompasses all the individual's mental and physical capacities-among older adults (aged ≥60 years) across diverse settings. The most effective exercise prescription strategies, and ongoing research gaps and implementation barriers, are also discussed. Evidence consistently supports multicomponent exercise programmes, including strength, aerobic, and balance training, as effective strategies to preserve or restore intrinsic capacity and overall functional ability in older adults, ranging from community-dwelling individuals to hospitalised individuals, individuals with frailty, or long-term care residents. Although the most pronounced benefits on intrinsic capacity are observed within the locomotion domain, improvements also extend to the cognitive, psychological, and vitality domains, particularly when exercise is part of a larger multidomain lifestyle intervention (eg, incorporating cognitive training or dietary interventions). In summary, exercise is a cornerstone intervention for healthy ageing, being effective across different levels of functional capacity and care settings. Efforts are needed to promote the widespread implementation of exercise programmes across diverse clinical, community, and care environments.

items.originalTitle: Mental health and psychosocial well-being of spouses of persons with schizophrenia: A systematic review
items.summary: BackgroundEvidence suggests that Spouses of Persons with Schizophrenia (SPwS) are susceptible to higher levels of caregiver burden, mental health problems, and poor psychosocial well-being compared to the general population. MethodologyA comprehensive literature search was conducted across six electronic databases.
items.caution: Strongest kind of evidence — still check who took part.
items.source: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
items.abstract: BackgroundEvidence suggests that Spouses of Persons with Schizophrenia (SPwS) are susceptible to higher levels of caregiver burden, mental health problems, and poor psychosocial well-being compared to the general population. The current review aimed to synthesize available evidence on the mental health, psychosocial well-being, and factors associated with the well-being of spouses of persons with schizophrenia.MethodologyA comprehensive literature search was conducted across six electronic databases. Studies published in English between 2000 and 2025 that met the inclusion and exclusion criteria were considered for the review. Screening, data extraction, and quality appraisal were conducted independently by the reviewers. The JBI Checklist for Analytical Cross-sectional Studies was used to appraise quality. Findings were synthesized narratively.ResultsFrom 1809, 23 studies, comprising 4116 participants from six countries, were included. The review identified moderate-to-severe levels of caregiver burden, high levels of psychological distress, and a higher prevalence of mental health problems among SPwS. Various patient and caregiver-related factors were strongly associated with higher burden and poorer mental health.ConclusionsThe findings highlight the need for routine assessment of spousal well-being and for the development of simple, culturally appropriate interventions for both patients and their spousal caregivers.

This study systematically reviews the association between mental health or behavioral factors and suicidal ideation among students in Africa.MethodsA comprehensive literature search was conducted to identify studies on the association between mental health or behavioral factors and suicidal ideation. We reported the review according to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Data were extracted into Microsoft Excel and analysed using Stata 17. Pooled associations were estimated using a random-effects model. The funnel plot and Egger's regression test were used to assess publication bias. Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis was conducted to assess the robustness of the pooled results. Results were displayed through tables and forest plots.ResultsWe included 49 studies involving 138,915 students. Students with depression and anxiety had 3.92 (95% CI: 2.05, 7.49) and 1.52 (95% CI: 1.45, 1.60) times higher odds of experiencing suicidal ideation than those without depression and anxiety, respectively. In addition, students who consumed alcohol, experienced loneliness, and felt hopeless had 1.38 (95% CI: 1.28, 1.49), 1.51 (95% CI: 1.33, 1.72), and 5.20 (95% CI: 1.99, 13.60) times the odds of experiencing suicidal ideation than their counterparts, respectively. Students who chewed khat, smoked cigarettes, used cannabis, and felt sadness had 2.12 (95% CI: 1.32, 3.42), 1.49 (95% CI: 1.39, 1.61), 1.44 (95% CI: 1.24, 1.66), and 1.76 (95% CI: 1.10, 2.81) times higher odds of experiencing suicidal ideation than their counterparts, respectively. Moreover, female students experienced suicidal ideation at 1.25 times higher odds than male students (95% CI: 1.18, 1.33). The pooled estimates showed substantial heterogeneity among the included studies.ConclusionThe findings indicated that anxiety, depression, loneliness, hopelessness, sadness, alcohol consumption, khat chewing, cannabis use, cigarette smoking, and being female were factors associated with suicidal ideation. Schools and universities are advised to prioritize mental health in educational settings by strengthening and improving mental health literacy, early identification of mental health concerns, reducing substance use, and providing access to counseling and social support networks.

items.title: Intimate partner violence and its association with mental disorders among women in the general population, pregnant women and postpartum women: systematic review and meta-analysis
items.originalTitle: Intimate partner violence and its association with mental disorders among women in the general population, pregnant women and postpartum women: systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major global health and human rights issue. However, the association between IPV and specific mental disorders across different life stages, including pregnancy and postpartum, remains insufficiently quantified.
items.caution: Strongest kind of evidence — still check who took part.
items.source: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science
items.abstract:
Background: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major global health and human rights issue. However, the association between IPV and specific mental disorders across different life stages, including pregnancy and postpartum, remains insufficiently quantified.

Aims: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to assess the associations between IPV and mental disorders among women in the general population, pregnant women and postpartum women.

Method: We searched six databases to identify cross-sectional, case-control and cohort studies published between 1 January 1980 and 13 June 2024. A random-effects meta-analysis model was performed to derive the pooled odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals.

Results: Of 7326 records identified, 82 studies with a total of 140 286 participants were included. For women in the general population, lifetime IPV was significantly associated with depression (odds ratio 2.26, 95% CI 1.83-2.79, p < 0.0001; class 1; moderate). Past-year IPV also demonstrated significant associations with depression (odds ratio 2.36, 95% CI 1.61-3.45, p < 0.0001; class 3; very low) and anxiety (odds ratio 2.85, 95% CI 1.61-5.05, p = 0.0003; class 3; low) among women in the general population. IPV during pregnancy was notably associated with depression (odds ratio 3.59, 95% CI 2.48-5.20, p < 0.0001; class 2; very low) and anxiety (odds ratio 3.27, 95% CI 2.60-4.10, p < 0.0001; class 1; moderate) in pregnant women. For postpartum women, lifetime IPV exposure was significantly linked to depression (odds ratio 2.09, 95% CI 1.54-2.83, p < 0.0001; class 3; moderate).

Conclusions: IPV is associated with depression, anxiety and eating disorders among women in the general population, pregnant women and postpartum women. Tackling the root causes of IPV and improving access to mental health services are critical steps in mitigating the long-term psychological burden on women worldwide.

items.title: The role of telehealth services in maternal mental health care access and satisfaction during the postpartum period
items.originalTitle: The role of telehealth services in maternal mental health care access and satisfaction during the postpartum period
items.summary: This systematic review examined the association between telehealth services and maternal satisfaction and access to mental health care during the postpartum period.
items.caution: Strongest kind of evidence — still check who took part.
items.abstract: This systematic review examined the association between telehealth services and maternal satisfaction and access to mental health care during the postpartum period. A comprehensive search of PubMed and SCOPUS using the key words: telehealth, maternal, satisfaction, postpartum and mental health yielded 347 articles published between 2015 and 2024. After applying inclusion criteria and screening through the PRISMA framework, 21 peer-reviewed U.S.-based studies were included, comprising a total of approximately 4077 participants. Studies included postpartum women of diverse racial, socioeconomic, and geographic backgrounds, with most conducted within the first year postpartum, although some extended from the early postpartum period (0-6 weeks) to up to two years after childbirth. Randomized controlled trials, cross-sectional surveys, mixed-method evaluations, and qualitative interviews were among the methods used in the reviewed studies. According to data analysis, telehealth services such as video consultations, mobile health applications, and remote therapy were associated with improved access to care by removing barriers such as transportation, childcare, and scheduling conflicts. Maternal satisfaction rates were high, with many studies reporting that 70-85% of participants found telehealth to be effective or convenient. Culturally appropriate and group-based interventions increased satisfaction, especially among African American and Latina mothers. However, limitations were identified, including issues with digital literacy, broadband access, and nonverbal communication. These factors have the potential to worsen current healthcare disparities, particularly in underserved communities. Despite these challenges, telehealth is feasible, acceptable, and effective for providing postpartum mental health care.This review encourages the use of hybrid care models and culturally sensitive telehealth interventions. Future research should explore the long-term outcomes and equitable strategies to expand telehealth for maternal mental health equity. Given the heterogeneity of study designs, including observational and descriptive studies, findings should be interpreted as associative rather than causal.

items.title: An astrocyte-microglia MFG-E8 axis promotes synapse engulfment in early amyloid pathology
items.originalTitle: An astrocyte-microglia MFG-E8 axis promotes synapse engulfment in early amyloid pathology
items.summary: Region-specific synapse loss is an early hallmark of Alzheimer's disease, yet the upstream signals that render synapses vulnerable remain unclear. In a mouse model of amyloidosis, we identify an early astrocyte state that emerges in vulnerable brain regions before widespread plaque deposition and overt gliosis.
items.caution: In animals or cells — may not carry over to people.
items.abstract: Region-specific synapse loss is an early hallmark of Alzheimer's disease, yet the upstream signals that render synapses vulnerable remain unclear. In a mouse model of amyloidosis, we identify an early astrocyte state that emerges in vulnerable brain regions before widespread plaque deposition and overt gliosis. These astrocytes exhibit bulbous-looking perisynaptic processes enriched in p62 and glycogen, impaired autophagic flux and calcium signaling, and diminished astrocyte-synapse coverage. Rather than exhibiting increased synapse engulfment, bulbous astrocytes show elevated milk fat globule-epidermal growth factor 8 (MFG-E8) and are associated with increased local microglial synapse engulfment. Astrocyte-specific gain- and loss-of-function experiments demonstrate that astrocyte-derived MFG-E8 is required for microglial synapse engulfment and acts through microglial β3 integrin signaling. Astrocytic Mfge8 deletion reduces microglial engulfment and synapse loss across amyloidosis models and is associated with reduced amyloid pathology, gliosis, and cognitive impairment. Together, these findings define an astrocyte-microglia MFG-E8 signaling axis that contributes to region-specific synaptic vulnerability during early amyloid pathology.
